analysis.headline: Colombia detains Mexican judge Luis Benítez Alcántara over an alleged $2 million Ryan Wedding bribe
analysis.what_happened: El País reports Colombia detained Mexico City judge Luis Benítez Alcántara. The United States seeks his extradition to California. El Universal reports he is accused of freeing a Ryan Wedding associate after a $2 million bribe.
analysis.says_vs_does: The charge is a US allegation of judicial sale, not a conviction. Sources do not record a Mexican court finding on the release itself.
analysis.follow_the_money: US authorities allege a $2 million bribe tied to Ryan Wedding's network. Sources do not give a date for the payment.
analysis.at_stake: A sitting Mexican judge faces a US extradition request over a release that favoured a trafficking associate. Wedding's network gains or loses a documented judicial channel.
tensions: US prosecutors vs Mexican judiciary: an extradition bid treats a Mexico City judge as a paid facilitator.
Wedding network vs enforcement: the alleged payment bought a release that US charges now reverse.

analysis.headline: Mexico City police seize 43 million pesos from China-born launderer Bojun 'El Chino'
analysis.what_happened: Excélsior and Proceso report federal and Mexico City forces detained Bojun, alias El Chino, in Miguel Hidalgo. They seized about 43 million pesos, including 920,000 dollars. El Gráfico links him to La Unión Tepito.
analysis.says_vs_does: Authorities call him leader of a laundering, arms and people-trafficking network across Mexico City, Tijuana and Cancún. That is an official claim pending charges.
analysis.follow_the_money: The raid recovered roughly 43 million pesos in cash, of which 920,000 dollars, per Excélsior and Proceso. Sources do not name the upstream payers.
analysis.at_stake: A cash-heavy Chinese-origin broker operating with a CDMX street gang loses a stash and a node. Cartel clients lose a local conversion channel.
tensions: Mexican authorities vs Chinese-origin cash brokers: a street seizure, not a bank case, hits physical proceeds.
La Unión Tepito vs federal forces: the reported link puts a local plaza next to a cross-city laundering claim.

analysis.headline: The Navy arrests CJNG plaza boss El Panda in Coatzacoalcos as RSF lists the cartel as a press predator
analysis.what_happened: Infobae and El Universal report Semar detained Samuel de la Cruz Anaya, alias El Panda, in Coatzacoalcos on 3 November. Outlets name him plaza boss for Jáltipan, Cosoleacaque and Minatitlán. Infobae reports Reporters Without Borders added the CJNG to its 2026 press-freedom predators list.
analysis.says_vs_does: Authorities link El Panda to kidnapping, extortion, drug sales and fuel theft. Those are Semar attributions. RSF's listing rests on documented attacks on journalists, not on this arrest.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure for El Panda's plaza revenue or for losses from the arrest.
analysis.at_stake: The CJNG, still in succession after El Mencho's death, loses another regional commander in the south. RSF's label marks the group's press violence as an international record.
tensions: Navy vs CJNG southern plazas: successive Veracruz and Oaxaca arrests cut into the same coastal corridor.
CJNG vs the press: RSF's predator listing treats journalist attacks as organisational practice.

analysis.what_happened: Primicias and Infobae report police detained 14 alleged Los Lobos members in Operativo Zeus 4. Interior Minister John Reimberg says more than 300 officers ran 25 raids across six provinces. Officials link the cell to 60 homicides and massacres in Los Ríos.
analysis.says_vs_does: Reimberg's toll of 60 killings is a police attribution. AP notes Los Lobos sit among groups the United States designates as terrorists.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure for the cell's extortion or trafficking take.
analysis.at_stake: Los Lobos lose an alleged hit squad while they and Los Choneros still contest export plazas. Noboa's interior ministry books a visible result under ongoing states of exception.
tensions: State vs Los Lobos: a multi-province raid targets a massacre cell rather than a port plaza.
Los Lobos vs Los Choneros: both remain the main contestants for Ecuador's cocaine export economy.

analysis.what_happened: El Espectador reports a Clan del Golfo–ELN dispute and the killing of Indigenous leader Ramiro Forastero and his son displaced about 500 people in Nuquí, Chocó. Pulzo places the flight in Villa Nueva.
analysis.says_vs_does: No stated peace claim from either armed group appears in these sources. The displacement record shows territorial fighting, not negotiation.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Coastal Chocó communities lose leaders and land to the same Clan–ELN contest that already shapes coca and migrant routes. The Clan's Antioquia expansion sits beside this Pacific pressure.
tensions: Clan del Golfo vs ELN: competition over Chocó territory produces forced displacement after a leader's killing.
Armed groups vs Indigenous authorities: the murder of Forastero and his son removes a local interlocutor.

analysis.headline: A Miami court sentences Venezuelan Jorge Figueira to 12 years for laundering more than $1 billion
analysis.what_happened: Infobae, citing the Miami Herald, reports Jorge Figueira, 60, received a 12-year sentence. He also accepted a $1 billion payment order. The Justice Department says the network ran from January 2024 to November 2025.
analysis.says_vs_does: The sentence and forfeiture order are court records. The $1 billion figure is the agreed payment order, not a traced cash inventory in these sources.
analysis.follow_the_money: Figueira laundered more than $1 billion for traffickers, with flows toward Colombia, China and Panama, Infobae reports from DOJ filings.
analysis.at_stake: A Miami-based Venezuelan broker loses liberty and faces a billion-dollar civil order. Trafficking clients lose a documented dollar-to-abroad channel.
tensions: US prosecutors vs Venezuelan money brokers: a plea converts a laundering claim into a 12-year term and a $1 billion order.

analysis.headline: An Ecuadorian court confirms asset seizures in the Blanqueo Fito case against Los Choneros' leader
analysis.what_happened: Primicias reports the tribunal notified its Blanqueo Fito judgment and upheld, with reservations, the confiscation of assets claimed by relatives of Los Choneros leader Fito. The court also ordered repatriation of capital from an international property.
analysis.says_vs_does: Family claimants sought to keep seized goods. The court kept the confiscation while noting limits, so the state's win is partial on the record.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a peso or dollar total for the seized assets. The judgment includes repatriation of capital from one foreign property.
analysis.at_stake: Fito's relatives lose a legal path to reclaim tied assets while he remains the Choneros figurehead in US custody. The state converts a laundering case into retained property.
tensions: Ecuadorian state vs Fito's family: confiscation stands despite relatives' claims on the same assets.

analysis.headline: US intelligence backed a Venezuelan drone strike on an ELN camp in Apure, and Washington is negotiating a long-term military deal with Caracas
analysis.what_happened: El País reports a drone strike on an ELN base in Apure, on the Colombian border, killed at least 20 people, citing human rights groups. La Silla Vacía and The New York Times report US officials say Washington supplied intelligence.
analysis.says_vs_does: Earlier reports framed the strike as a Venezuelan army action, while El País calls it a US antidrug war on Venezuelan soil. La Silla Vacía separately names Tren de Aragua chief Niño Guerrero in Bolívar state as a target, so accounts of the operation differ.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The post-Maduro government gains standing with Washington by hitting a guerrilla it long hosted. CiberCuba and BAE Negocios report talks on a permanent US military presence, after a joint June strike killed Tren de Aragua founder Héctor Guerrero Flores.
tensions: Venezuelan state vs ELN: a former rear-guard host now strikes the guerrilla with US help.
US vs Tren de Aragua: joint strikes have now targeted its founders inside Venezuela.

analysis.headline: Forced recruitment across four states feeds the Sinaloa Cartel's civil war as Mazatlán closes its deadliest month
analysis.what_happened: El Universal reports a forced-recruitment network feeding the Sinaloa war from Jalisco, Zacatecas and Durango. Disappearances of non-residents in Sinaloa rose from 142 in 2023 to 231 in 2025, a 63% increase.
analysis.says_vs_does: Mazatlán mayor Estrella Palacios calls security 'a challenge' after October passed 100 homicides, Ríodoce reports. Ríodoce also reports a severed head left with a message addressed to her father.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure for recruitment payments or the factions' war spending.
analysis.at_stake: Both factions replace losses with outside recruits, and Infobae reports cells defecting from the Chapitos to seek new alliances. Culiacán's bishop says a priest was held and tortured for three days by captors seeking faction information.
tensions: Chapitos and CJNG vs Mayiza: El Universal links the Jalisco–Zacatecas route to the Chapitos–CJNG alliance and the Durango route to the Mayiza.
Factions vs the Church: torturers sought intelligence on Chapitos and Mayiza from a priest, the bishop says.

analysis.what_happened: Milenio reports El Semáforo, the presumed successor of El Tanque in the CJNG, was detained in Tuxtepec, Oaxaca, 23 days after his former boss's capture. The Navy reports hits on CJNG, Los Salazar and Cártel de Guasave leaders between 14 and 28 October.
analysis.says_vs_does: Antonio Oseguera, Tony Montana, pleaded guilty to drug and weapons charges and asks for 20 years, citing health and age, Milenio and Infobae report. The Navy's tally is its own claim of results.
analysis.follow_the_money: The Navy values two Sinaloa seizures of vehicles, weapons and drugs at 6.182 million pesos, an official estimate of losses to the groups. Sources do not give other figures.
analysis.at_stake: The CJNG, in succession since El Mencho's death, keeps losing regional commanders in quick succession. Oseguera's sentence sets the US price for a founding family member who pleaded guilty.
tensions: Navy vs CJNG: successive arrests in Oaxaca hit the same regional command twice in under a month.

analysis.what_happened: Voz reports a US federal court sentenced Wenshen Xu, a 52-year-old Chinese citizen, to 12 years. His network moved more than 450 kilograms of cocaine into the United States and laundered more than $22 million.
analysis.says_vs_does: Mexico's Finance Ministry says the FATF evaluation that just ended reflected its anti-laundering efforts, El Economista reports. That is a government claim; the FATF's own findings are not in these sources.
analysis.follow_the_money: Over $22 million in drug proceeds was laundered through Xu's network on behalf of CJNG trafficking, according to the sentencing reported by Voz. Sources do not give dates for the flows.
analysis.at_stake: The case adds a court record to US claims that Chinese brokers launder cartel revenue. Mexico's FATF rating affects how foreign banks treat Mexican correspondent accounts.
tensions: US prosecutors vs Chinese money brokers: a conviction rather than a designation ties a Chinese national to CJNG proceeds.

analysis.says_vs_does: President De la Espriella says 'the false total peace has ended'. El Tiempo reports high-value targets remain out of reach, and a truck bomb hit a police station in El Tambo, Cauca, on Wednesday.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The surrender law offers armed groups a legal exit while the state escalates. The Antioquia government reports the Clan del Golfo in 94 municipalities, up 40 since 2022.
tensions: Government vs FARC dissidents and ELN: attacks on police and toll booths in the southwest continue, with three toll attacks in under a month.

analysis.headline: Brazil's Senate passes the public security amendment unopposed as federal police target a PCC-linked group that moved R$500 million
analysis.what_happened: The Senate approved without opposition a constitutional amendment widening the federal government's security role against factions such as the PCC and CV. Revista Oeste reports the Federal Police targeted a PCC-linked group on the Paraguay border.
analysis.says_vs_does: Senators present the amendment as a blow to the factions, while the Federal Police case shows police officers suspected of aiding the PCC-linked scheme.
analysis.follow_the_money: The PCC-linked group allegedly moved R$500 million and ran drug routes to Europe, Revista Oeste reports. Sources do not give dates for the flows.
analysis.at_stake: Brasília gains authority over a security field held by the states. In Bolivia, police report expelling 65 PCC and CV leaders, while one faction still operates in Santa Cruz, Beni and the Chapare.
tensions: Federal government vs PCC: a border network with alleged police help sits inside the new federal mandate.

analysis.what_happened: Primicias reports El Oro has broken its homicide record, with Puerto Bolívar holding 11% of the killings and 300 families displaced. Police and Interior Ministry reports identify a Los Choneros and Sao Box alliance in Machala, Pasaje and Santa Rosa.
analysis.says_vs_does: President Noboa governs through states of exception three weeks before elections, Estrella Digital reports, yet official reports show violence rising in El Oro.
analysis.follow_the_money: Official reports cited by Primicias put drug sales points at USD 2,000 a day. Sources do not give a provincial total.
analysis.at_stake: Puerto Bolívar is an export port, so control of local plazas also bears on cocaine shipments. Ecuador has extradited nine nationals since a 2024 referendum allowed it.
tensions: Los Choneros and Sao Box vs Los Lobos and Lobos Espejo: they compete for Machala, Pasaje and Santa Rosa.

analysis.headline: A year after Carlos Manzo's killing, investigators tie the Uruapan mayor's murder to CJNG revenge and count 34 detained
analysis.what_happened: Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo was shot dead on 1 November 2025 by a 17-year-old, and authorities attribute the killing to the CJNG. El País and Infobae report an encrypted chat, a hard drive and 34 detentions, including people from his close circle.
analysis.says_vs_does: Excélsior reports investigators call the case 90% solved and describe it as CJNG revenge for the August 2025 arrest of plaza boss René Belmontes, El Rhino. Sources here do not say whether whoever ordered the killing has been charged.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The CJNG, in succession since El Mencho's death, lost its Uruapan plaza boss before the killing and dozens of operatives after it. Manzo's family and movement remain split over his political legacy, Contramuro and the Los Angeles Times report.
tensions: CJNG vs Uruapan's local government: the mayor confronted the group directly during his year in office, Milenio reports.
State prosecutors vs FGR: the federal prosecutor did not take over the case, according to Excélsior.

analysis.headline: Marina arrests El Semáforo, named as El Tanque's successor in the CJNG, in Tuxtepec, Oaxaca
analysis.what_happened: The Navy arrested Carlos César Cruz Muñoz, alias El Semáforo or Señor de las Luces, in San Juan Bautista Tuxtepec, Oaxaca, La Jornada and El Financiero report. The Security Cabinet said alleged CJNG logistics operator Ana Gabriela Aguilar Ávalos was also detained.
analysis.says_vs_does: Authorities call him the CJNG plaza boss for Veracruz-Boca del Río and El Tanque's direct successor. That label is an official claim; corridos cited by Milenio and Infobae celebrated his rise before any charge.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The federal government shows a second blow to the same CJNG regional command within a month, after El Tanque's arrest on 5 October. The CJNG loses another Gulf-coast manager during its succession.
tensions: Federal forces vs CJNG Gulf command: two successive regional chiefs have fallen since 5 October.

analysis.headline: Colombian police and the FBI arrest two Mexicans described as the CJNG's main links to the Clan del Golfo
analysis.what_happened: Colombia's National Police and the FBI arrested two Mexican nationals, alias La Patrona and La Pau, in Barranquilla on 28 October, El Tiempo and Proceso report. They are held for extradition to the United States.
analysis.says_vs_does: Police describe them as the two main links between the CJNG and the Clan del Golfo for large cocaine shipments. Sources show no charging documents yet, so the role rests on police statements.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The arrests target the supplier relationship between Colombia's largest armed group and a Mexican buyer, not street distribution. The CJNG loses brokers at the point where cocaine changes hands.
tensions: CJNG and Clan del Golfo vs joint US-Colombian enforcement: the arrests hit the wholesale link between producer and buyer.

analysis.headline: Sheinbaum acknowledges a rise in Sinaloa homicides as federal security chiefs tour the state
analysis.what_happened: President Sheinbaum said homicides in Sinaloa have risen in recent days and that she sent the Security Cabinet to the state, La Jornada and Milenio report. Milenio counted at least 13 dead in one day.
analysis.says_vs_does: Sheinbaum says intelligence analysis has been done to explain the rise. The visible response is supervision visits by Trevilla in Mazatlán and García Harfuch at Culiacán's C4i, not a new announced operation.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The federal government seeks to show control over a war now past two years. A house reportedly used as Governor Rocha Moya's campaign office was shot at on 26 October in Culiacán.
tensions: Chapitos vs Mayiza: the homicide rise follows the killing of Chuy González and arrests in the Chapitos arms network.

analysis.headline: Ecuador arrests the mayor of Vinces in a 3.2 million dollar laundering case tied to Los Choneros and Los Lobos
analysis.what_happened: Police arrested the mayor of Vinces with 12 others for a hearing and four for investigation, Primicias and Infobae report. Ecuador also extradited to the US two men tied to the Villavicencio killing and a Los Choneros leader.
analysis.says_vs_does: Prosecutors allege links to Los Choneros and Los Lobos and to the Gran Fénix, Cantabria and Metástasis cases. These are accusations awaiting a charging hearing, not convictions.
analysis.follow_the_money: The investigation covers 3.2 million dollars in alleged laundering. Primicias reports the mayor's construction company grew its assets 570% during his term; sources do not name the payers.
analysis.at_stake: Noboa's government shows reach into local officials who allegedly serve the gangs it declared terrorists. The gangs lose a municipal channel for moving money through public works.
tensions: Ecuadorian state vs Choneros and Lobos: enforcement now targets the officials and firms that launder gang revenue.

analysis.headline: Colombia carries out the sixth bombing of De la Espriella's government, killing six
analysis.what_happened: The armed forces bombed a camp before dawn on 28 October, leaving six dead and one captured, Caracol Radio and El Tiempo report. Troops seized ten rifles, a grenade launcher and ammunition.
analysis.says_vs_does: De la Espriella announced the strike in advance and called it very important and strategic. Outlets disagree on the target: Caracol places it in Chocó against the Clan del Golfo, while one El Tiempo report names Mordisco's dissidents.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The president gains a show of force after loosening some restrictions on bombings, Yahoo Noticias reports. La FM reports that an earlier bombing in his term killed four dissidents, including a 16-year-old.
tensions: Colombian state vs Clan del Golfo and FARC dissidents: air strikes have returned as a routine tool under the new government.

analysis.what_happened: Chile's PDI arrested two Venezuelans and a Chilean over the kidnapping and killing of a 45-year-old woman found in a Puente Alto camp, BioBío and Cooperativa report. Four jailed suspects face new charges.
analysis.says_vs_does: The Clinic reports the faction's members came from earlier Tren de Aragua cells dismantled in other cases. Arrests have broken cells without ending the brand, which regroups under new names.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Kast's government faces pressure as Justice Minister Rabat confronts a constitutional accusation over sentence reductions for Tren de Aragua extortionists. The case undercuts its hard-line message.

analysis.headline: Rio police target a Comando Vermelho gas-cylinder monopoly as Mato Grosso do Sul arrests PCC and CV members
analysis.what_happened: Operação Dominus targeted a Comando Vermelho group in Rio de Janeiro that imposed a monopoly on cooking gas, G1 reports. In Mato Grosso do Sul, police served 20 arrest warrants over the PCC-CV dispute.
analysis.says_vs_does: The record shows the CV acting as a tax and market authority in areas it controls, forcing traders to meet sales targets. This goes beyond drug trafficking into control of household goods.
analysis.follow_the_money: The group charged 150 reais per gas cylinder and set sales quotas for merchants, G1 reports. Sources do not give a total revenue figure.
analysis.at_stake: The CV draws steady income from residents regardless of drug markets. Brazilian police seek to cut that revenue, while the PCC and CV compete for territory in Mato Grosso do Sul.
tensions: PCC vs Comando Vermelho: the MS investigation identified 22 people involved in the two factions' dispute.

analysis.headline: US charges 24 in a Sinaloa-linked Tennessee network run from state prisons, as CBP reports large port seizures
analysis.what_happened: US prosecutors charged 24 members of a network linked to the Sinaloa Cartel that distributed meth, fentanyl and cocaine in Tennessee, Infobae reports. CBP seized nearly 1,600 pounds of meth at Otay Mesa.
analysis.says_vs_does: US authorities link the Tennessee network to the Sinaloa Cartel. Sources name no faction, and two leaders allegedly ran it from state prisons, which points to local control.
analysis.follow_the_money: CBP valued the Otay Mesa meth at 2.5 million dollars and a Brownsville cocaine load at 611,000 dollars. Seizure values are agency estimates and measure enforcement as well as traffic.
analysis.at_stake: US prosecutors show reach into retail distribution. Commercial trucks at ports of entry remain the documented crossing method in these cases.
tensions: US enforcement vs cartel supply: seizures concentrate at commercial crossings in California and Texas.

analysis.headline: Marina kills Chuy González Peñuelas, Cártel de Guasave figure wanted by the US, in northern Sinaloa
analysis.what_happened: Navy forces killed Jesús González Peñuelas, alias Chuy González, after a pursuit in Siete Ejidos, Guasave, according to Ríodoce and El País. Security Secretary García Harfuch said two men died and identification awaits genetic and fingerprint tests.
analysis.says_vs_does: Harfuch places him in the Cártel de Guasave under Fausto Isidro Meza. Outlets report he worked for both the Chapitos and the Mayiza, so his allegiance in the civil war is contested.
analysis.follow_the_money: The US offered a reward of 5 million dollars. Expansión reports that US authorities linked him in May to drug trafficking and laundering for the Sinaloa Cartel; sources do not give laundering figures.
analysis.at_stake: Mexico gains a high-value result on a US most-wanted target before federal security chiefs tour Sinaloa. His network's northern Sinaloa heroin and fentanyl production loses a senior manager.
tensions: Chapitos vs Mayiza: outlets disagree on which faction González Peñuelas served when he died.

analysis.headline: Chihuahua governor accuses Morena leader Ariadna Montiel of crime ties, and the Security Cabinet denies any intelligence report
analysis.what_happened: Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos told Carlos Loret that Morena leader Ariadna Montiel has ties to organised crime, citing a meeting involving El Guano. The federal Security Cabinet denied the meeting and any intelligence report.
analysis.says_vs_does: Both sides offer claims, not evidence. Campos has shown no documents in sources, and the federal denial came by social-media message; Montiel is preparing three legal complaints against Campos.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Campos gains a national platform against Morena in a state contested by Sinaloa factions. Montiel and the federal government seek to contain a narco-politics charge against the ruling party.
tensions: Chihuahua government vs federal government: the PAN governor and Morena trade accusations, and Guanajuato's PAN governor declined to back Campos.

analysis.what_happened: US authorities arrested 10 alleged members of a Sinaloa Cartel affiliate in Florida, including cell number two Erick Manuel Gómez Tapia, alias El Canelo. CBS12 describes a cocaine pipeline from Mexico to Tampa Bay.
analysis.says_vs_does: US authorities call the cell a Sinaloa Cartel affiliate. Milenio notes that no cell name has been released and nothing ties it to the Chapitos or the Mayiza.
analysis.follow_the_money: CBS12 values the bust at 30 million dollars. Sources do not show how proceeds moved back to Mexico.
analysis.at_stake: US prosecutors show reach into cartel distribution inside the United States. The affiliate loses its Florida distribution cell.
tensions: US enforcement vs Sinaloa distribution: arrests hit the retail end of the supply chain, not its Mexican command.
